Read Today's Paper Muthoot Finance Q2 cons profit jumps 36% YoY to Rs 3,278 crore SECTIONS Muthoot Finance Q2 cons profit jumps 36% YoY to Rs 3,278 crore By Atmadip Ray , ET Bureau Last Updated: Oct 31, 2026, 06:15:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Muthoot Finance reported a 36% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 3,278 crore in Q2, while assets under management grew 42% to Rs 2.09 lakh crore. However, standalone gross NPA ratio rose to 3.87% from 2.28% in the previous quarter, indicating a deterioration in asset quality Reuters For 9 months, profit after tax surged 91% year-on-year to Rs 7,048 crore, compared with Rs 3,693 crore in the corresponding period last year. Kolkata: India's largest gold loan company Muthoot Finance reported a 36% year-on-year surge in consolidated net profit for the second quarter at Rs 3,278 crore, backed by 42% expansion in business while asset quality deteriorated. The net profit was Rs 2,412 crore in the year ago period. On a standalone basis, the company's second quarter net profit stood at Rs 2977 crore, up 27% over Rs 2345 in the year-ago quarter. Muthoot's consolidated assets under management grew 42% year-on-year to Rs 2.09 lakh crore at the end of September. Out of this, the gold loan stood at Rs 1.93 lakh crore. Its standalone AUM grew at the same pace to Rs 1.88 lakh crore, of which gold loan was Rs 1.79 lakh crore. Live Events The company's standalone gross non-performing assets ratio jumped to 3.87% at the end of September from 2.28% three months prior. Muthoot's subsidiary Belstar Microfinance earned a Rs 78 crore net profit for the quarter under review, widening from Rs 66 crore in the first quarter. Its asset quality improved with gross NPA ratio falling to 3.26% from 4.58% a year back. Its first half net profit stood at Rs 144 crore compared to a loss of Rs 160 crore in the year-ago six month. Its AUM stood at Rs 7,876 crore at the end of September against Rs 7,715 crore a year prior as industry-wide stress moderated disbursement growth, the company said.
